sources.name: OWR 44/2008 Discrete Geometry
sources.paraphrased_findings: The connected-set model specifies a separator and four tangents, two internal and two external, for each pair. Definition 2 encodes directed tangent events. Question 1 gives the imported target and an affirmative attribution. Problem-session item 12 prints four weak state axioms and separately requests polygonal output referring to the fully separated term. No proof is supplied there that all four-axiom inputs contain that term. No n>=3 or pairwise-distinct-state restriction was found.

sources.name: Goodman-Pollack November 26 2006 author manuscript
sources.render_note: Poppler emitted Type 3 glyph bounding-box warnings. Rendered pages were legible; primes, ordered-switch formulas, Proposition 10, Corollary 11 and Definition 12 were visually checked.
sources.paraphrased_findings: The model in Theorem 1 has four tangents and one separator per pair. Definition 9 constructs words from directed switches. Proposition 10 requires the stronger switch properties. Corollary 11 has only four state properties. Definition 12 explicitly names Corollary 11, and the adjacent universal realization question likewise asks about its conditions. Neither definition adds separated-start, switch-once, distinct states, or a lower bound excluding two bodies.

sources.name: Dhandapani-Goodman-Holmsen-Pollack April 21 2005 author manuscript
sources.paraphrased_findings: Page 4 writes each switch in its before-move order. Page 5 calls a cyclic sequence simple when each move contains one ordered pair and separately defines allowable through switch-once supporting/separating events. Page 6 exhibits a two-body half-period with repeated states, so repeated terms are not generally excluded. The stronger definition rejects the corrected witness.
